caption.text:
There’s a specific kind of heartbreak that doesn’t come from losing someone — it comes from slowly losing yourself while trying to keep them.

You don’t notice it at first. You just start shrinking in small ways. Saying less. Wanting less. Needing less. You call it compromise, patience, understanding… but really, you’re editing your personality so you’re easier to love. You start becoming a softer version of yourself, not because you’ve grown — but because you’re afraid that being fully you is “too much.”

And the painful part? Even after all that bending, they still don’t meet you where you are. You change… and they stay the same. You move backward trying to hold on, while the relationship keeps asking you to disappear just a little bit more.

Love isn’t supposed to cost you your identity. It’s not meant to make you question your worth, dim your personality, or feel like you have to earn basic care. The right love doesn’t ask you to become smaller — it gives you space to expand. It feels warm. Safe. Like you can exhale and still be chosen.

Sometimes walking away isn’t giving up on love — it’s choosing yourself so you don’t have to abandon who you are just to be loved.

📖 ‘Beauty In The Stillness’ by Karin Hadadan (find it by following the link in our bio)
